question: Which Pratihara ruler successfully repelled Arab invasions in North-Western India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagabhata I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nagabhata I** was a ruler of the Pratihara dynasty who ruled during the 8th century CE.
 
• He is credited with successfully repelling the Arab invasions of North-Western India, particularly the forces of the Umayyad Caliphate.
 
• These invasions were led by the Arab general **Junaid**, who sought to expand the Caliphate's rule in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Nagabhata I's victory prevented the further penetration of Arab forces into North India, securing the region from external threats.
 
• This event is a significant milestone in Indian history, as it marked the containment of Arab expansion in the Indian subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pratihara Dynasty:** The Pratiharas were a prominent Rajput dynasty in India, known for their resistance against external invasions and their contributions to art and architecture.
 
• **Umayyad Caliphate:** The Umayyad Caliphate was an early Islamic empire that expanded rapidly from the Middle East to parts of Europe and Asia, including attempts to invade India.
 
• **Battle Strategy:** Nagabhata I employed effective military strategies and alliances to counter the technologically advanced Arab forces.
 
• **Gurjara-Pratiharas:** Nagabhata I was the founder of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, which later played a key role in unifying Northern India during the early medieval period.
 
• **Historical Context:** The Arab invasions were part of a larger movement of Islamic expansion during the 8th century, but Nagabhata I's resistance ensured that North-Western India remained predominantly Hindu during this period.
